title: Level 1 (Beginner) - B-5
notes:
West leads the ♠J against 6NT. South has 8 top tricks (3 spades, 3 hearts, and 2 clubs). After winning the opening spade lead, South must play on diamonds to come to 12 tricks. South starts by playing a diamond towards the dummy. When West follows low, South must decide whether or not to play dummy's ♦K.

Playing dummy's ♦K will succeed when East has a singleton Queen of diamonds or when East was dealt Queen doubleton of diamonds. In the latter case, the ♦Q and ♦A will crash on the second round of the suit.

Playing dummy's ♦J (or any other diamond besides the ♦K) will succeed any time West has the ♦Q. South can return to his hand and finesse twice more if necessary. Finessing against West's ♦Q is actually the percentage play. Remember that when you have a 9 card fit missing just the Ace and Queen, finesse against the Queen, not the Ace.
